title: Quarterly account storyline & slide samples — Standard + Enterprise
content:
Purpose: This doc is a lightweight, storyline-driven QBR deck template with two variations: Standard (mid-market / SMB accounts) and Enterprise (multi-stakeholder, contract-renewal focus). Use as a living draft to adapt slide counts, data depth, and asks by account maturity.

How to use: pick the appropriate storyline (Standard vs Enterprise). Keep temperature low for exec-facing slides (clear metrics + one-line ask). For technical deep dive, append an appendix with runbooks, SLOs, and performance traces.

Core narrative arc (both variants):
- Hook: 30s summary — ARR impact / key win or risk
- Health snapshot: usage, latency, cost per inference, support volume
- Value delivered: top 3 product wins tied to business outcomes
- Adoption plan / roadmap alignment: upcoming product changes that matter to this customer
- Risks & mitigations: capacity, quality regressions, security/compliance items
- Asks & next steps: commercial, technical, operational (clear owner + date)

Standard slide sequence (recommended 8–10 slides):
1) Title + meeting objectives (1 line each) — Speaker note: confirm time and attendees
2) 30s exec summary: ARR influence, health score (green/amber/red) — Note: avoid >3 metrics
3) Usage trends (30/90/180d): API calls, peak QPS, embeddings volume — Graph: small multiples by product area
4) Latency & error surface: p50/p95, token cost trend, notable incidents last quarter — Note: call out improvements after tuning
5) Success stories: 2 bullets of customer outcomes with before/after numbers
6) Adoption opportunities: recommended pilots + expected impact (deltas as ranges)
7) Renewal checklist & timeline: current term, renewal window, proposed path to close
8) Ask slide: clear request (e.g., budget approval, access, exec intro) + owners
9) Appendix: config recommendations, tickets referenced

Enterprise slide sequence (recommended 12–16 slides, stakeholder layers):
1) Title, meeting objectives, attendees and decision owners (capture procurement/legal contacts)
2) One-line value statement tied to business KPI (e.g., reduce support deflection by X% = $Y)
3) QBR TL;DR: bullet bullets — health, churn risk, renewal date, required commitment
4) Multi-dimension health matrix: adoption by team, performance by region, security posture (checks)
5) Economics deep-dive: token-level cost breakdown, reserved vs burst capacity savings, recommended commit
6) Reliability & incidents: timelines, root causes, mitigation actions, SLO adherence
7) Roadmap alignment: features landing in next 90/180 days and what it unlocks for the customer
8) Migration/runway plan: steps to move workloads to Dedicated or Private if requested
9) Contract options & pricing scenarios: base case, upsell case, urgency incentives (only 1 slide)
10) Risk register: 3 highest risks, owners, escalation path
11) Ask and decision points: approvals needed this quarter (legal, procurement, exec sponsor)
12) Project plan & next steps: owners, dates, success criteria
13) Appendix: technical appendix, logs, benchmark snippets, tickets

Renewal tracker (light text table — paste into sheet for automation):
Columns: Account | Current ARR | Renewal window | Renewal owner | Health score | Primary risk | Recommended path | Next meeting date | Decision needed
Example rows:
Acme Corp	$220k	2025-06-15	Leah Martinez	Amber	Latency at scale	Dedicate pool pilot	2025-03-04	Budget approval
Nimbus Inc.	$45k	2025-04-01	Priya Rao	Green	None	Standard renewal with 10% uplift	2025-02-20	None

Speaker tips and micro-scripts:
- Exec opener (30s): "In the last 90 days we delivered X that moved your Y metric by Z; today we want to confirm the path to scale that outcome."
- When showing risk: call out customer impact first, then technical cause, then our mitigation and ask.
- Pricing ask script: show economics slide, then say: "To hit the target throughput and cost profile we recommend committing to X; this yields estimated savings of Y%. Who on your side owns procurement?"

Support artifacts to attach in slide pack:
- Recent SLO dashboard screenshot (p95, errors)
- Token-cost waterfall for the account (last 90d)
- Top 5 API endpoints by volume and latency
- Open ticket summary (IDs + status)

Common pitfalls to avoid:
- Too many slides with raw logs — move to appendix.
- Overly technical slides for execs (summarize first, details later).
- Late asks — surface decision points early in the deck.

Working checklist before sending deck: send deck 3 business days before meeting; include pre-read summary; tag legal/procurement on pricing slides (enterprise).

Open questions (for CS ops & product):
- Should we standardize the Enterprise economics slide with our new committed-tier SKU? (Marcus to follow up; refer JIRA:CUST-332)
- Do we need a one-click sheet export of the renewal tracker? (PRI: product ops)

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal; copy into account-specific folder and tailor per customer (replace generic graphs with account data).

File history: v0.1 draft 2024-10-18 initial idea; v0.3 2025-02-12 added enterprise pricing scenarios and renewal tracker example.
